summary: In this excerpt from Cory Doctorow's novel Little Brother (labeled 'Book 1 — part 82'), the narrator Marcus wakes his friend Jolu with repeated calls and then secures a chat over Xnet after learning the radio vans may be watching them. Jolu proposes a cover story: a teenage party at the Sutro Baths, where trusted friends can meet to do a key-signing for a web of trust. The excerpt closes with a passage on handling a spy by feeding him misinformation rather than exposing him.
one_line: Marcus and Jolu plan a disguised key-signing party at Sutro Baths to build a trusted encrypted network after suspecting surveillance.
key_facts: The narrator woke Jolu by ringing his cell phone and hanging up after the first ring, three times in a row.
Jolu was sent to the narrator's blog-post about the radio vans and came back worried, asking 'You sure they're looking for us?'
The narrator sent Jolu to a quiz, and Jolu responded 'OMG we're doomed.'
Jolu estimated he could totally vouch for about 20 or 30 people.
A web of trust is a crypto method that allows trusted people to talk securely without others listening in, but it requires physically meeting the people in the web at least once.
Jolu suggested disguising the key-signing as a teenage party so there would be a ready-made excuse if anyone asked questions.
Jolu proposed holding the party at the Sutro Baths.
The narrator's ARG team were described as his closest friends.
The narrator says Darryl 'would know' how to organize the meeting, as it was the kind of thing he was great at.
The passage contrasts denouncing a spy with intercepting his communications and feeding him and his masters misinformation.
The example given is having the spy follow the narrator around while his masters believe he is gathering information on the narrator's movements.
